original_question: Design a polynomial-time algorithm that decides whether a given graph admits pretty good state transfer between two vertices, and also design an algorithm that computes a subsequence of times witnessing that phenomenon. Here pretty good state transfer between vertices u and v means that there are distinct times t for which the sequence (|exp(it_j A)_{uv}|)_{j >= 0} converges to 1, where A is the adjacency matrix of the graph.
target_in_paper: Section 2.3 ("Bonus problems related to state transfer"), Open Problem 2.4: find a polynomial-time algorithm to test whether pretty good state transfer occurs, and an algorithm to compute a subsequence of times witnessing it.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's actual target. It captures the same two algorithmic tasks as Open Problem 2.4: a polynomial-time decision procedure for pretty good state transfer and a separate procedure for producing witness times. It also uses the correct continuous-time evolution exp(i t A) and the correct convergence criterion |(exp(i t_j A))_{uv}| -> 1 for pretty good state transfer.
missing_details: The paper's local definition is for a fixed pair of vertices, so the input should be made explicit as a finite graph G together with specified vertices u and v (implicitly distinct).
The times t_j should be stated to be real numbers, and the witness sequence should consist of pairwise distinct real times.
To be fully stand-alone, define the continuous-time quantum walk operator as U(t) = exp(i t A(G)), where A(G) is the adjacency matrix of G, and then state the condition as |U(t_j)_{uv}| -> 1.

The phrase "graph admits pretty good state transfer" is ambiguous unless one says whether this means between the given pair u,v or for some unspecified pair; in this context it should mean between the designated vertices u and v.

The paper only requires polynomial time for the decision algorithm; for the second task it asks more generally for an algorithm computing a witnessing subsequence of times, not explicitly a polynomial-time one.

If the algorithm returns witness times, the success condition should be stated explicitly: on yes-instances it outputs a sequence (or, in the paper's wording, a subsequence) (t_j) such that |(exp(i t_j A(G)))_{uv}| converges to 1.

No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency conditions are relevant here; the hidden assumptions that matter are instead the finite graph setting, the adjacency-matrix Hamiltonian, and the real time parameter.
refined_question: Given a finite graph G with adjacency matrix A(G) and two distinct vertices u,v in V(G), find a polynomial-time algorithm that decides whether pretty good state transfer occurs between u and v, in the sense that there exists a sequence of pairwise distinct real times (t_j)_{j >= 0} such that |(exp(i t_j A(G)))_{uv}| converges to 1 as j -> infinity; and, whenever the answer is yes, find an algorithm that computes such a witnessing sequence of times (equivalently, a subsequence of times representing pretty good state transfer, in the paper's wording).
justification: This draft is targeting Open Problem 2.4 almost verbatim. The paper first defines the continuous-time quantum walk by U(t) = exp(i t A(G)) in the introduction, then immediately before Open Problem 2.4 defines pretty good state transfer between vertices u and v by the existence of a sequence of distinct times (t_j) for which |(exp(i t_j A(G)))_{uv}| tends to 1. Open Problem 2.4 then asks for exactly two things: a polynomial-time test for whether pretty good state transfer occurs, and an algorithm to compute a subsequence of times witnessing it. The main refinement needed is to make the fixed input pair (G,u,v), the real-time sequence, and the witness-output condition explicit. The paper itself does not state an alternate equivalent formulation of this open problem.
